claims.heading: ## 1. Context: why edge-triggered mode exists
claims.claim: Several widely used event loops register with ET: the Go runtime ✅[^go]
claims.context: Why anyone wants ET: an LT loop that is not ready to consume a descriptor, for example a socket that is writable while there is nothing to send, gets it back on every call. ET reports it once and stays quiet. The cost is a stricter contract: the application must consume everything that is available, because the kernel will not remind it. Several widely used event loops register with ET: the Go runtime ✅[^go], mio (the I/O layer under the Tokio async runtime for Rust) ✅[^mio], and nginx for client connections ✅[^nginx].
